A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ROS framework. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial formatting and presentation changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original ROS experiments on random regular graphs, Gset, COLOR, perturbed edge weights, and component and sampling ablations.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results and reports additional Bitcoin-OTC, weighted-Gset, Max-10-Cut, and baseline comparisons.

M1.justification: The probability-simplex relaxation, GNN architecture and objectives, pre-training/fine-tuning procedure, and categorical sampling algorithm remain unchanged. Testing additional values of k and graph distributions does not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: V2 adds the Bitcoin-OTC trust network and Max-10-Cut, with corresponding 7-regular training graphs. It extends weighted-Gset testing to k=3 and substantially broader weight distributions. COLOR and mild Gset perturbations were already evaluated in v1 Appendices D and F.

E2.justification: V2 adds ECO-DQN and removes Rank2 and ECORD from reported comparisons. ANYCSP already appeared in v1's appendices, but v2 adds it to random-regular and Max-3-Cut comparisons and expands its Gset participation. These are substantive comparator changes, not merely updated citations.

E3.justification: Added experiments specify 500 training graphs with 100 nodes and degree 7 for k=10, additional uniform weight-multiplier ranges [0,10] and [0,100], and T=0 sampling-study reference entries. The ten perturbed instances per graph and existing ROS architecture, optimization settings, and stopping criteria are retained.

E4.justification: The existing mild edge-weight perturbation study expands into three perturbation regimes and includes Max-3-Cut, substantially broadening robustness analysis. V2 Tables 12 and 14 also add T=0 reference values to the sampling studies. The earlier GNN-versus-MLP component ablation remains in Appendix F.

E5.justification: V1 Tables 15–16 report means and standard deviations for mildly perturbed Gset cut values and runtimes. V2 Table 8 and Figure 4 omit those uncertainty estimates, while retaining the ten-instance construction. Random-regular uncertainty reporting remains; no increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive results for new settings and comparators and revises existing entries. PI-GNN's N=1,000 Max-Cut mean changes from 1263.95 to 1210.45 in v1 Table 1 versus v2 Table 2. ROS's COLOR-david k=3 value changes from 338 to 324. All 71 Gset PI-GNN score/time pairs change, while the corresponding ROS entries remain unchanged. Results under new weight distributions are additional evaluations, not same-setting gains.

T1.justification: V1 Theorems 1–2 and their appendix proofs correspond to v2 Theorems 3.2–3.3 and Appendices B–C. Their assumptions, conclusions, and proof arguments are retained; numbering and optimal-solution notation change without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain a scalable framework for arbitrary signed edge weights, relaxation/sampling consistency, fast solution of large graphs, and generalization. Mentioning real-world datasets in the abstract and conclusion broadens the supporting evidence without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations connecting ECO-DQN's scaling costs to per-decision GNN computation and ANYCSP's runtime to global search and long sampling trajectories. It removes the ECORD failure discussion. The existing pre-training tradeoff and interpretation of ANYCSP's difficulty with weighted graphs remain.

D1.justification: The code-access address changes from an anonymous repository to the named NetSysOpt/ROS repository. V2 documents additional dataset construction and ANYCSP's default time limit, but drops v1's NetworkX generator instruction and Python 3.8.19 version. Core ROS hyperparameters and GPU information remain.

R1.justification: New Appendix A and Table 5 systematically position simplex relaxation against Lovasz, SDP, rank-2, and QUBO alternatives across complexity, applicability, consistency, and scalability. The introduction adds substantive discussion distinguishing NeuroCUT, DGCLUSTER, and DMoN from Max-k-Cut methods. These changes exceed bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most methodological exposition remain. V2 rewrites experimental descriptions, integrates COLOR and weighted-Gset discussion into the main narrative, reorganizes appendices, and replaces many 'objective value' labels with 'cut value.' Publication information, an impact statement, and acknowledgements are added.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figure 2 is recomposed and expanded to three panels; Figure 4 adds weighted-Gset runtime displays. New dataset and relaxation-comparison tables appear, COLOR results are consolidated with Bitcoin-OTC, and benchmark tables gain or lose comparator columns.

improvement.justification: Beyond v1's existing COLOR and mild-perturbation tests, Bitcoin-OTC, Max-10-Cut, stronger perturbations, and broader neural comparisons provide useful validation of ROS's claimed applicability. The expanded research positioning also helps assessment. These gains are limited by removed perturbation standard deviations and unexplained discrepancies between updated PI-GNN results in v2 Table 6 and retained values in Tables 10–11.
